_meta.author: Peter Higgins + Claude (Cowork session)
_meta.purpose: User-acceptance test packet for the Hs repository. Where CLAIM_TEST_PACKET validates that the scientific claims numerically hold (MC-4.C1 Aitchison-native, etc.), this packet validates whether a stranger arriving at the repo can find their way, run an analysis on their own data, verify a published number, and report back. This is the apparatus test, not the science test.

sibling_packets.claim_test: ai-refresh/CLAIM_TEST_PACKET.json — validates scientific claims (MC-4 conjuncts, IEEE-floor confirmations)

execution_modes: human — community member walks the phases manually with the .md companion
ai_assistant — Claude/ChatGPT/Grok/Gemini executes against a live repo connection
automated — a shell script in the future could check the deterministic phases
_meta.promotion_rule: STAGED on first arrival. Promoted to CANONICAL after at least two independent testers (different ENV classes per CROSS_AI_COORDINATION.md §2) complete all seven phases without blocking issues.
_meta.scope_note: This packet tests the repo as it ships to outsiders. It does NOT test the conference-internal materials (talk delivery, speaker prep, lockdown discipline) — those have their own SPEAKER_BRIEF.md governance.

S-A.title: First-time CoDa researcher
S-A.background: Knows Aitchison geometry, CLR, ILR. Has never heard of Higgins Decomposition. Arrived from a CoDaWork 2026 abstract or a colleague's mention.
tools_assumed: ability to read English mathematical prose
S-A.success_criteria: Within 15 minutes, can articulate what CNT computes, what CNQ adds, and where to find a worked example.

S-B.title: AI assistant cold-read
S-B.background: ChatGPT / Claude / Grok / Gemini given the repo URL with no prior context. Asked to summarise the project for the user.
S-B.success_criteria: Within five fetches, has loaded HS_FAST_REFRESH.json + AI_AGENTS.md + treasure map + at least one engine README, and can answer the grounding-test challenge in AI_AGENTS.md §3 correctly.

S-C.title: Conference attendee with phone open
S-C.background: Sitting in the CoDaWork 2026 audience. Opens the QR code on the printed handout during the talk.
S-C.success_criteria: Can follow CONFERENCE_ATTENDEES.md slide-by-slide and open the interactive projector in the browser without leaving the page.

S-D.title: Researcher with their own dataset
S-D.background: Has a CSV — e.g., a 10-column budget allocation over 25 timesteps, a 6-component industrial yield series, or a 9-column geochemical assay through time. Wants to know what Hs would say about it.
tools_assumed: willingness to confirm a carrier-meaning mapping
S-D.success_criteria: Within one CCTT run, has produced a hash-verifiable CNT JSON + Stage 1 plate + journal entry on their own data, and can articulate what Power Share and Activation Coefficient say about that data.

phases.title: Discovery and entry
phases.objective: Within 60 seconds of landing on the repo, the tester knows what Hs is, what it computes, and where to read next.

steps.looking_for: tagline, what-is-this paragraph, AI-loader badge, conference-status callout pointing to CODA-Association/
current_commit_sha, last_push, engine versions (CNT v3.1.0 / CNQ v2.0.0), conference window dates

steps.action: Open the discovery channel for AI

feedback_questions: Did the README tell you what Hs is within 30 seconds of reading?
Was the AI-loader badge visible and did it explain itself?
Was the path from repo root → CONFERENCE_ATTENDEES.md → projector navigable without backtracking?
Any dead links, stale dates, or wrong slide counts?
failure_modes: README tagline is too abstract or doesn't say 'compositional'
Engine versions in README disagree with HS_FAST_REFRESH.json
Handout PDF link 404s
Slide-count drift across surfaces (the push #55 fix should have closed this — verify it stuck)

phases.title: Refresh validation
phases.objective: Confirm HS_FAST_REFRESH.json is consistent with the live HEAD of main.

steps.expected: matches git rev-parse HEAD on main (or the API equivalent)
describes the most recent commit narratively + cites SHA + CI run number + duration
the most recent push entry there matches HS_FAST_REFRESH
exit 0; all green per DCP-001 verified status

feedback_questions: Did current_commit_sha match the live HEAD?
If not, was the cache-lag note in AI_AGENTS.md §2.1 visible enough to prevent panic?
Did the consistency checker (if you ran it) report any drift?
Was the push number sequence in PUSHES_INDEX.md continuous (no missing entries)?
failure_modes: current_commit_sha lags the actual HEAD (cache lag — known issue, expected to clear)
AI connector reports a SHA different from what HS_FAST_REFRESH says (genuine drift — file a DCP)
Consistency checker reports errors (genuine drift — review the DCP-001 evidence pattern)
PUSHES_INDEX has a gap (admin sync missed a push)

phases.title: CoDaWork 2026 package usability
phases.objective: From a phone or laptop, the tester can attend the talk virtually using just the CODA-Association folder.

steps.looking_for: slide-by-slide layout, every slide links to its supporting evidence
single page, QR code present, USA Solar 760× headline, 5-of-9 signature, contact line
loads offline; RADAR / BARY / ALIGN modes all functional; SHOCK overlay highlights Japan 2011→2012 and Germany 2013–2014 reorganisation
325 pages; 9 country sections × 6 plates each; hash-chain present on the cover
Nature-structure with cover + TOC; six figures present including Fig 6 navigation chart; Supplementary Information accessible

feedback_questions: Could you follow the talk slide-by-slide from CONFERENCE_ATTENDEES.md alone?
Did the projector load in your browser without any network call? (Disconnect from Wi-Fi to verify.)
Were all three projection modes responsive (RADAR / BARY / ALIGN), and did SHOCK highlight Japan 2011 → 2012?
Did the handout fit on one A4 page when you printed it?
Did the manuscript render cleanly, including Figure 6?
failure_modes: Projector tries to fetch external resources (would fail offline)
Manuscript Figure 6 fails to render (caption-table overlap fixed in push #52 — verify it stuck)
Handout overflows to page 2 (line-spacing tune in v8 should have closed this)
Slide count in attendee page disagrees with deck

phases.title: Handbook and vocabulary lookup
phases.objective: When the tester encounters an unfamiliar term, the path to its definition is obvious and the definition is correct.

steps.looking_for: v3.0 header; ~220 entries; 30 sections; merge note (push #54, 2026-05-19)

steps.expected: PCA, SVD, eigenvalue, Spectral Theorem all have standalone entries in §1
CLR, ILR, Helmert basis, Aitchison geometry all have entries in §3
Helmsman, Power Share, Activation Coefficient, yeast factor, MC-1 through MC-4 all defined
81-line stub pointing to GLOSSARY.md v3.0; no v2.0 content lingering
§28 of GLOSSARY contains CHSH, EITT, MORB, OIB, BTL, RWA, DADC, …

feedback_questions: If you encountered 'Activation Coefficient' in the manuscript with no prior context, could you find its definition in under 30 seconds?
Are there any terms in the talk, projector, or handout that are NOT in the glossary? (List them — that's the priority gap.)
Does any glossary entry contradict the manuscript or speaker brief?
Did you find the redirect stub or did you end up reading the legacy v2.0 content by mistake?
failure_modes: Term used in manuscript but missing from glossary (file a gap for the next merge)
Glossary entry contradicts the engine's actual computation (file a high-priority DCP)
Notation stub still has v2.0 content (push #54 was supposed to fix; verify)

phases.title: User data pipeline — the CCTT 7-phase walk-through
phases.objective: Researcher S-D arrives with their own CSV. Within one CCTT run, they have a hash-verifiable CNT JSON + Stage 1 plate + journal on that CSV.
prerequisites: pip install -r requirements.txt (or pip install . per pyproject.toml)
A CSV with: a time column (year, date, or ordered index) + 3–16 carrier columns that sum to a constant per row, OR raw counts that can be normalised to a composition

steps.expected: User identifies: time column, carrier columns, units (percent / fraction / count / mass), expected closure

steps.action: Match against the 13-adapter registry or build a one-file adapter
steps.user_confirms: carrier-meaning mapping (column X means carrier Y)

steps.expected: schema 3.1.0 output with cnt_content_sha256; finishes in seconds for small CSV

steps.action: Select Stage 1 (always) + any of Stage 2 / 3 / 4 / spectrum / projector based on data shape
steps.looking_for: tools/MissionCommand or run_experiments.py for the multi-plate driver

steps.action: Re-run the engine; SHAs must match bit-for-bit
steps.user_confirms: ship / no-ship decision based on whether the result looks meaningful

steps.action: Write a JOURNAL.md describing the dataset, the carrier mapping, the headline finding, and any caveats
steps.expected: the JOURNAL.md is what a reviewer would read first

feedback_questions: How long did Phase 1 take (diagnosing the CSV)?
Did the 13-adapter registry have a near-match for your data, or did you need to build a new adapter?
Did cnt.py run without errors on first try? If not, what was the error message and was it actionable?
Was the Stage 1 plate readable to someone who hadn't seen it before?
Did the second engine run produce identical SHA-256 hashes?
If you wrote a JOURNAL.md, did the template/example you used come from inside the repo or did you have to invent it?
What was the single biggest friction point in the 7 phases?
failure_modes: Adapter registry doesn't cover an obvious common domain (file as a deferred adapter request)
cnt.py errors on edge cases (zeros, missing values, single-row, ragged time)
Stage 1 plate fails to render or is illegible at default size
SHA mismatch on second run (this would be a major issue — engine determinism is a doctrine)
User has no idea what to put in JOURNAL.md (missing template)

phases.title: Reproducibility verification
phases.objective: Tester picks one published number from the manuscript or speaker brief and re-derives it from the repo.

steps.path: data/ember/ or DATA/* per the input doctrine

steps.action: Locate the engine that produced it

steps.expected: the exact same number emerges (within IEEE machine floor)
the chain from raw CSV → CNT JSON → plate → manuscript figure resolves end-to-end

feedback_questions: Which number did you target?
Did your re-run produce the same number to IEEE-floor precision?
If not, what was the discrepancy magnitude and was it explainable (e.g., engine version drift, locale, BLAS)?
Could you trace every artefact in the chain back to a SHA-256?
failure_modes: Source CSV is referenced but not present in the repo (data licensing — should be documented)
Engine version used for publication ≠ engine version currently shipping (engine_version_policy in data_outputs/README addresses this; verify it's findable)
Re-run produces a meaningfully different number (genuine reproducibility failure — file as a DCP)

phases.title: Feedback loop
phases.objective: Tester knows exactly how to report a confusion, bug, or suggestion back to the project.

steps.action: Find the investigation catalog entry workflow
steps.expected: describes how a new INV entry is proposed; references CCTT and OPERATIONS_PROTOCOL
issue templates or at least a README pointer
cross_check_archive append rule for AI-generated reviews

feedback_questions: If you found a confusing passage in the manuscript, where would you report it?
If you found an engine bug, what's the right channel — GitHub Issue, INV catalog entry, or direct email?
If you're an AI assistant that produced a useful review, where does that review get archived?
Is the path from 'I spotted something' to 'it's now tracked' under three clicks?
failure_modes: No clear contribution path documented (community uptake will stall)
Investigation Catalog has high barrier to new entries (good — preserves rigor — but should be documented)
AI-assistant archive folder is hidden / undiscoverable
